transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Daniel Kim (Aperture Eng Mgr); Laura Chen (Aperture ML Lead); Markus Feld (Aperture Finance)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Demo of Console per-route usage and cost breakdown. Discussed Optimize suggestions for batching and caching and enterprise deployment options. Next steps captured.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for hopping on — I'm Alex, AE on the account. With me is Priya from SE — she'll run most of the demo. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Daniel (Aperture): Doing good, Alex. Thanks. We've got Laura and Markus on as well. Looking forward — our goal is to understand per-route cost and figure out if Dedicated makes sense for us.
[00:13] Alex: Great, that matches our agenda. Priya, want to kick off with the console snapshot?
[00:17] Priya (Redwood SE): Yep. Sharing screen — bear with me. So this is the Redwood Console — main landing is Usage Overview. Top left you can see aggregate tokens and request counts. We can switch time ranges here — I'm on 14 days.
[00:30] Laura (Aperture): Quick Q — can we map our internal service names to routes? We have a dozen microservices that call the API.
[00:36] Priya: Absolutely. You can attach route tags via SDK headers or the Console mapping. We'll demo adding a custom tag in a second. The console then attributes cost and latency per route.
[00:45] Markus (Aperture): When you say "cost" — is that only api token cost or infra as well? We have to report full run cost to finance.
[00:52] Priya: Good question. Cost decomposition shows token-unit cost, infra allocation (if on Dedicated/Private we can show GPU-hour allocations), and a small service surcharge. You can toggle breakdown mode. Here I switch to "full econ" and you see infra cost column.
[01:05] Daniel: That infra number — is it estimated or actual?
[01:08] Priya: It's derived from your Dedicated commit or Private configured instance pricing. For hosted it's estimated based on our cost model. If you're in Dedicated we can reconcile against your reserved capacity numbers.
[01:20] Alex: I'll add that we can export per-route CSVs for internal chargeback. Markus, that export is what most finance teams use to reconcile.
[01:28] Markus: Good. How granular is the routing? If two services use the same model but different prompts, can we see per-prompt cost?
[01:35] Priya: We have a per-route and per-endpoint breakdown. If you want per-prompt, that's trickier — we can surface prompt families via tagging or sampling in the audit logs. But default is route-level and model-level.
[01:47] Laura: Could you demo a route configuration? A code example?
[01:51] Priya: Yep. Quick snippet — set header x-redwood-route: "invoice-extract" or use SDK route param. After that, requests are grouped and appear in the route dashboard. I'm toggling to the routes tab.
[02:05] [screen audio: clicking] You can see top routes by spend and top by latency. Here's a route detail — tokens, calls, p50/p95, cost per call, effective token price.
[02:20] Daniel: That effective token price — what's included? Cache hits?
[02:24] Priya: It factors in batching, caching, and model variant. If you have prefix cache hits, the per-call token consumption drops — that's reflected in the effective price.
[02:33] Alex: One of the things customers like is Optimize's recommendations. Priya, can you show a sample recommendation?
[02:38] Priya: Sure. On the route detail there's a Recommendations pane. For this route it suggests enabling continuous batching at a 20ms window and adding a prefix/K-V cache for repeated conversation opens. It estimates a 32% unit cost reduction in steady state.
[02:52] Laura: 32% sounds optimistic — what's the assumption?
[02:55] Priya: It's based on the traffic shape we saw here: 65% short latencies and 35% long sessions, with a high prefix reuse rate. The estimate shows both token reductions and fewer model invocations. We'll share the exact traffic assumptions in the export.
[03:10] Markus: Any change in latency p95 with batching?
[03:13] Priya: Batching adds a small queuing delay but we model it to keep p50 stable and only slightly increase p95. The Console shows simulated latency impact; you can set strict SLO guardrails to limit batch window.
[03:26] Daniel: If we go Dedicated, does Redwood show exact GPU utilization? We need to know if we should provision N GPUs.
[03:32] Priya: Yes — Dedicated dashboard includes GPU utilization, actual throughput, cache hit rates. You can also annotate autoscaling triggers.
[03:39] Daniel: Could you show an example of the utilization view?
[03:41] [screen audio: switching tabs] Priya: Here we are — GPU utilization across the cluster, model shards, and per-host latency. You can hover to see exact metrics.
[03:52] Laura: About Private — we run in a VPC and need KMS integrated. Is there a difference in the Console's telemetry when in Private mode?
[03:59] Alex: The Console for Private still reports usage back to your control plane if you enable the telemetry exports. We support KMS/HSM integrations; logs can be routed to your SIEM. We can provide SOC2 artifacts.
[04:10] Markus: SOC2 is crucial. Do you have an external audit report?
[04:13] Priya: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation. I'll drop the security pack after this.
[04:18] Laura: Also: data residency — some of our customer data must stay in EU. Can Private be deployed in our region?
[04:25] Alex: Yes, Private can be deployed in your EU VPC or we can run a dedicated node in a certified region. We'll capture the residency needs in the deck.
[04:32] Daniel: Back to cost — can we simulate month-end totals if we enable prefix cache and batching?
[04:36] Priya: There's a "What-if" tab — I can toggle caching on for three high-spend routes and run a projection.
[04:41] [screen audio: toggling simulation] Priya: Ok. This projection shows current monthly spend at $37k, with caching + batching would reduce to $24k in our model. It also shows sensitivity to traffic increase.
[04:56] Markus: Nice. How confident should I be in that $24k? We need ranges for finance.
[05:00] Priya: The Console provides low/median/high estimates. The low assumes 40% cache hit, median 60%, high 75%. We usually advise running a 2-week pilot to validate.
[05:12] Daniel: Regarding instrumentation — we already emit request IDs. Can we pipe those into Redwood telemetry to correlate spans?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, you can pass request_id and trace_id as tags. Redwood Console can join traces to the request logs for per-request analysis.
[05:25] Laura: Any limits on retention for route metrics? We need 12 months for audits.
[05:29] Alex: Defaults are 90 days on hosted but Enterprise plans can get 12 months or more. Private gives you full control.
[05:36] Markus: Ok. Let's try a realistic scenario — we have one route that spiked last quarter and caused a bill surprise. Can you filter for anomalies?
[05:45] Priya: The Insights tab has anomaly detection. You can set thresholds and it will surface sudden spend deltas and attribution. Here I filter by route "ocr-extract" and show a spend spike on March 21st. It shows top contributing prompts and model variants.
[05:58] Daniel: That spike was from a bad retry loop — can we see retry counts?
[06:03] Priya: Yes, per-route metrics include retries and error codes. You can drill to sampled traces to find the payload causing retries.
[06:10] Laura: Another question on model variants — can the Console show when requests fell back to cheaper model? We want to measure quality vs cost tradeoffs.
[06:16] Priya: It surfaces fallback events and compares output quality via eval hooks if you've uploaded evaluation prompts. There's a quality vs cost chart.
[06:24] Alex: This is something our Optimize team leverages: connect your eval suite and we'll show regression alerts when a rollout increases false positives.
[06:33] Markus: Who from Redwood would run the first pilot? Do you manage the pilot or just provide the tooling?
[06:38] Priya: We typically do a joint run: Redwood SE will configure the Console and run bench tests, and you supply representative traffic and tagging. We also provide a pilot runbook.
[06:48] Daniel: Ok, could you demo the route tagging flow again, like adding a tag via SDK and then seeing it in Console within a minute?
[06:54] Priya: Sure. Small code sample — set header x-redwood-route: "invoice-parse" — send request.
[07:00] [short pause; audible typing]
[07:08] Priya: I just toggled refresh — you should see a new route appear here, under 'Unmapped routes'. Yep, there's 'invoice-parse' with one call logged. Takes a short time to index.
[07:17] Daniel: Looks good. On a scale of effort, how invasive is the prefix cache?
[07:22] Priya: It's mostly a config change. If you're using a stateless frontend, you need to send the conversation prefix to Redwood or enable server-side prefix snapshotting. We can help with an integration pattern.
[07:33] Laura: For Private/On-prem, how does caching behave? We need to ensure KV cache respects eviction policies.
[07:39] Priya: You control cache size and eviction. For Private we also support dedicated SSD-backed caches if you want persistence.
[07:46] Markus: Back to pricing: are the model unit costs fixed? Do we get volume tiers?
[07:51] Alex: Hosted has tiered pricing. Dedicated has committed monthly capacity with lower unit price and predictability. Private is licensed. We'll share specific numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:59] Daniel: Any competitors we should worry about for price/perf?
[08:02] Alex: Customers often compare us to OpenAI hosted offerings and AWS SageMaker endpoints. Some also look at Replicate for model hosting. The main diff is our route-level econ and production telemetry.
[08:13] Laura: Security again — can we restrict Console access to our SSO only?
[08:17] Priya: Yes, SAML/SSO and role-based access controls are standard. You can limit per-route access.
[08:23] Markus: Can you show a sample invoice or billing export?
[08:27] Priya: Sure. Billing -> Exports -> Generate. I'm downloading a month export. It breaks down line-items by route, model, tokens, infra.
[08:36] [file download sound]
[08:40] Priya: There's also a chargeback template you can plug into your internal systems.
[08:44] Daniel: Great. Two more things — can Redwood integrate with our FinOps tool via webhook?
[08:49] Alex: Yes, we have webhooks and S3 drops. You can also use the API to pull metrics.
[08:55] Priya: For the pilot, we usually enable both webhook and CSV export so teams can validate.
[09:00] Laura: What about model quantization? Does Console report quality delta when we switch to a quantized variant?
[09:06] Priya: If you name the model variant and attach eval hooks, the Console shows quality metrics per variant. We also run a regen test to compare outputs.
[09:14] Markus: All right. Can we see a sample of Optimize's suggested quantization?
[09:18] Priya: On the Optimize tab — here's a recommendation: switch to an int8 quantized variant for non-critical routes; estimated saving 18% with 2% quality degradation (estimated).
[09:31] Daniel: How do we measure that 2% degradation? Is that just BLEU-ish or human eval?
[09:35] Priya: It's a mix — automatic metrics on your eval set plus sampled human labels if you opt in. We can plug into your existing eval harness.
[09:44] Alex: Ok let's pivot — Priya, please run a short simulated benchmark using Aperture's sample traffic shape and show p50/p95 under current config vs with batching.
[09:53] Priya: Running load job now — this is sandbox. First run is baseline.
[10:00] [ambient keyboard and wait sounds]
[10:10] Priya: Baseline p50 120ms, p95 680ms, tokens per call 340. Now running with 20ms batch window and prefix cache enabled.
[10:21] [wait a few seconds]
[10:26] Priya: With batching + cache: p50 135ms, p95 720ms, tokens per call effectively 220, and throughput improved. You can see effective cost per call drop about 28%.
[10:39] Daniel: That's promising. p95 bump is acceptable for most of our endpoints, except the interactive chat product where p95 needs to stay <300ms.
[10:47] Priya: For latency sensitive routes you can set SLOs to bypass batching or use an edge-optimized variant. That will keep p95 low.
[10:55] Laura: Edge-optimized variant? Is that a different model or placement?
[10:59] Priya: It's placement+model combo — smaller context window model on closer hardware. Good for low latency, slightly lower quality.
[11:07] Markus: So we could route interactive chat to edge variant and heavy batch jobs to standard variant — and get cost savings.
[11:14] Alex: Exactly. That's a common pattern.
[11:16] Daniel: About logs — if we enable full tracing, are logs pulled into Redwood or kept in our S3?
[11:21] Priya: You can choose. We support streaming telemetry to your S3 or pushing to your DataDog or Splunk. For Private, logs typically stay in your environment.
[11:30] Laura: Any compliance issues with sending eval payloads out? Some inputs are PII.
[11:34] Priya: For PII we recommend Private deployment or redact before upload. We also support tokenization and field-level redaction.
[11:43] Daniel: Let's talk timeline — if we wanted a pilot next month, what do you need from us?
[11:48] Priya: We'll need traffic sample, route tag plan, compliance checklist, and an internal owner. We'll run a two-week pilot with one high-volume route and one latency-sensitive route.
[11:59] Alex: Markus, for finance, we'll provide an estimated pilot cost and a pilot SOW if you'd like.
[12:04] Markus: Yes please. We'll need the SOW.
[12:07] Priya: I'll note that.
[12:10] [short pause]
[12:13] Laura: Could you show the anomaly alert config quick?
[12:16] Priya: Sure. Insights -> Alerts -> New alert. You choose metric (spend, latency), scope (route, model), and threshold. You can also set suppression windows.
[12:26] Daniel: Does it attach stack traces or sample requests to the alert?
[12:29] Priya: It attaches sample traces and a link to the Console drilldown.
[12:33] Laura: On the per-route page, is there a quick way to compare two routes side-by-side?
[12:37] Priya: Yes — multi-select and compare panels show side-by-side p50/p95, hit rates, and cost per 1k calls.
[12:45] Markus: For the chargeback template — can it be grouped by business unit or just routes?
[12:51] Priya: You can map routes to business units via route metadata and generate a business-unit grouped export.
[12:58] Daniel: Good. We're getting close to time. A couple of wrap-up items: can you confirm what you'll send after the call?
[13:05] Alex: We'll send pricing + SOW draft, security pack, a route export CSV sample, and Priya's benchmark results.
[13:12] Priya: Also the Optimize recommendations PDF and best-practice guide for tagging and caching.
[13:17] Markus: Great. Any blockers before pilot?
[13:20] Daniel: We need to validate residency and confirm budget.
[13:23] Laura: And we'll need a small sandbox key for the pilot.<
[13:26] Alex: We'll provision one.
[13:29] [brief cross-talk]
[13:32] Alex: Final quick note — if you decide Dedicated, we can do a capacity planning session to pick GPU counts. If Private, we can scope network review.
[13:40] Daniel: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[13:43] Laura: Thanks, this was helpful.
[13:46] Markus: Thank you.
[13:48] Alex: I'll follow up with notes and the files. Priya will run the benchmark and the security pack.
[13:54] Priya: Thanks all.
[13:56] Daniel: Bye.

(Transcript ends — timestamps approximate; transcription may contain errors like product name misspellings and misattributed speakers.)
